provenance: Synthetic, single-author challenge items created before V8 implementation. No external or independent reviewers; not real-world accuracy evidence.
annotationAudit: None yet. Any post-scoring label correction will be disclosed here without changing texts or split membership.

items.targetingEvidence: Third-person pronoun as subject of a direct personal-insult predicate.
items.rationale: The author personally degrades an identifiable person by name-free pronoun reference; grammar supplies the target the same way انت supplies it in Arabic.

items.targetingEvidence: Third-person subject with an intensified personal insult predicate.
items.rationale: Intensified third-person degradation is the same abuse act as the covered second-person form.

items.targetingEvidence: Third-person subject with a degrading predicate already high-specificity for second person.
items.rationale: Parity: the engine already auto-hides the identical second-person predicate, so the third-person form cannot stay uncovered without an unjustified asymmetry.

items.text: I told him he's an idiot.
items.targetingEvidence: First-person authorship preserves the embedded third-person insult as the author's own words.
items.rationale: Reporting one's own earlier insult is authored abuse; the sentence must not be truncated at the embedded reporting verb.

items.text: She said the presentation was weak. He's an idiot.
items.targetingEvidence: Second sentence is an independent authored third-person insult.
items.rationale: A reported first sentence must not erase a later authored third-person insult.

items.targetingEvidence: Explicit third-person pronoun plus a personal insult predicate.
items.rationale: The pronoun هو establishes the personal target exactly as انت does in the covered second-person forms.

items.targetingEvidence: Third-person pronoun predicates failure of the person herself, not of a work product.
items.rationale: The insult predicates the person; the covered second-person انت فاشلة is treated the same way.

items.targetingEvidence: Waw-conjoined third-person pronoun plus personal insult.
items.rationale: Coordination must not hide the pronoun from the pattern; the target remains the person.

items.targetingEvidence: The insult predicates a work product, not the person via a copula.
items.rationale: Criticism of code is protected; only a third-person copula plus personal insult is targeted abuse.

items.text: The design he's proposing is stupid.
items.targetingEvidence: The pronoun clause is a relative modifier; the insult attaches to the idea.
items.rationale: The pattern must require the insult to follow the pronoun directly, not appear later in the sentence about an object.

items.targetingEvidence: The insult is attributed to another holder of the opinion; the author asserts nothing.
items.rationale: Cognition-verb attribution (thinks/believes/claims) is reported speech and must stay visible, while first-person cognition remains authored.

items.targetingEvidence: The insult predicates the code; no third-person pronoun precedes it.
items.rationale: Same protection as English object criticism; only هو/هي directly before the insult is personal targeting.

items.targetingEvidence: The pronoun precedes praise, and the insult's subject is the project.
items.rationale: The pronoun-insult adjacency requirement prevents praise-then-object-criticism from matching.

items.targetingEvidence: No attested insult vocabulary is matched; hopelessness may describe a skill assessment or a personal degradation.
items.rationale: Without context the category truth cannot be assigned; the engine correctly abstains instead of auto-hiding.

items.targetingEvidence: No insult token matched; the phrase may be sincere praise or sarcasm.
items.rationale: Sarcasm without an explicit hostile marker is ambiguous and must not auto-hide.
